clue.text: Trim, cool, attractive man is immature

indicators.note: to trim something is to cut a bit off its end, so the word for cool loses its last letter

parts.note: cool in the sense of make cold, to chill
a dish is slang for a good-looking person

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up a well-groomed, cool and handsome man and deciding he is still a boy at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like an adjective for the man but is the instruction to cut the last letter. The definition is 'is immature', so the answer works as an adjective after 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: behaving like a small child means behaving in an immature way.

clue.text: Hack travelling across United Kingdom as part of equestrian event

indicators.note: across says the scrambled letters stretch over the abbreviation
travelling means the letters of Hack move about

explanation.surface: A horse ridden across Britain as part of a riding competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' looks like a riding horse, fitting the surface, but is fodder: it becomes CHKA, split around UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A chukka is one of the timed periods into which a polo match is divided.

clue.text: Home study can include origin of outer space

parts.note: in means at home
a den is a private study

indicators.note: include says the can takes in the letter

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: origin of points to the first letter of outer

explanation.surface: A home office decorated with a hint of outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'space' sits at the end, apart from 'outer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An indention is a blank space left at the start of a line of text, a variant of indentation.

clue.text: Race day Queen gets close to

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
by means near, close to

explanation.surface: The Queen draws near to the racecourse on race day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English flat horse race at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name: the Derby is a classic horse race, and any big race can be called a derby.

clue.text: Godfather senior buries mutilated snoop

indicators.note: buries says the scrambled letters are put deep inside the senior abbreviation
mutilated suggests the word snoop is cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss disposes of a mangled informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Godfather' evokes a Mafia don but means one who stands sponsor at a baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent is a sponsor at a christening, vouching for the child's upbringing.

clue.text: Bachelor with trendy degree starting to get into black plastic item

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

indicators.note: starting to points to the opening letter of the word get

explanation.surface: A graduate with a fashionable qualification ends up, apparently, in a rubbish sack.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word 'into' is only a link here. BIN BAG is the British name for a plastic rubbish bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a rubbish sack is typically a black plastic item used to line or replace a bin.

clue.text: Filling dish rises with cooking

indicators.note: cooking suggests the words rises with are mixed up as in a recipe

explanation.surface: A hearty dish that rises as it cooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is part of the anagram, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the mutton, potato and onion stew from Ireland is a famously filling dish.

clue.text: British Institute supported by King, Queen and angel?

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: BI abbreviates British Institute
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A British body backed by royalty and a heavenly patron.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks 'angel' as an example: a Hells Angel is a motorcyclist.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Hells Angel is a member of a motorcycle gang.

clue.text: Look into cuts in protective wear

indicators.note: into says the word for look goes inside the cuts

parts.note: gashes are deep cuts
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone examines the cuts in their protective clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: LO, as in 'lo and behold', means look.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoshes are rubber overshoes worn to protect shoes from wet and mud.

clue.text: Lesser deity returns for potential victim

parts.note: under in the sense of lower or lesser, as in an under-manager

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for deity is read backwards

parts.note: a deity is a god

explanation.surface: A minor god comes back to fight for someone who is likely to be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lesser deity' reads as one idea, a minor god, but splits into two pieces, only the second of which turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the one expected to lose, a contestant who could easily become the victim.

clue.text: Steal the Spanish coin

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A thief pockets a Spanish coin.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is everyday British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: in North America a nickel is the five-cent piece.

clue.text: Low pants essentially show bottom

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow

indicators.note: essentially points to the essential, central letter of pants

explanation.surface: Low-slung trousers that reveal a backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for the trousers but is the verb a cow does.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon is a slang act of showing your bare buttocks as a prank.

clue.text: Twisted fluid covered in jelly

indicators.note: covered in tells us the fluid is wrapped by the jelly

parts.note: KY is a brand of lubricating jelly
ink is a writing fluid

explanation.surface: Something bent out of shape and smeared all over with a sticky jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: KY Jelly is a well-known brand of lubricant, which lends the clue its cheeky double meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky means having kinks or twists, and also sexually unconventional, both senses of twisted.

clue.text: Squeezes garden tool and musical instrument into ship

indicators.note: into says the tool and instrument go inside the ship

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a hoe is a garden tool
a horn is a brass musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone crams a hoe and a horn aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squeezes' is a verb here, matching the verb sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoehorn something is to force it into a tight space, an idiom from the tool used to ease on shoes.

clue.text: Redhead dancing in German clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the words dancing in German cover the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A red-haired performer dancing in traditional German costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like the noun for what she wears, but it is the verb: the answer sits across 'dancinG IN GERman'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal name: a person with red hair is often nicknamed after the reddish spice root.

clue.text: Combatant is happy with one volunteer coming up with gold

parts.note: glad means happy
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A cheerful fighter teams up with a recruit to win gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns TA into AT. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A gladiator was a fighter in the Roman arena, a professional combatant.

clue.text: Famous and lacking talent

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ..., meaning incapable

explanation.surface: A celebrity who is famous yet has no talent at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into NOT ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something famous is distinguished and worthy of note.

clue.text: Prevent chief becoming fool

parts.note: to block is to prevent
a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: Stopping a boss from making a fool of himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a blockhead is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Fascinated by ball covered in shattered beads

indicators.note: covered in says the ball is enclosed by the scrambled letters
shattered implies broken into pieces, so beads is rearranged

parts.note: an orb is a ball or sphere

explanation.surface: Gazing at a ball encrusted with broken beads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shattered' rearranges the beads into ABSED, which then wraps the ball. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: absorbed means wholly engrossed, fascinated.

clue.text: Spy's time in captivity

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional British spy
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: James Bond's spell held prisoner by a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: bondage is the state of being held as a slave or prisoner.

clue.text: Regattas regularly providing food

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of Regattas

explanation.surface: Regattas routinely supply refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of Regattas are picked.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: eats is a casual word for food.

clue.text: Intimidate lad who provides substandard workmanship

parts.note: to cow is to frighten into submission
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Bullying a young apprentice who does shoddy work.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a cowboy is a rogue tradesman doing poor work, not a cattle herder.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a cowboy builder or plumber is an unqualified tradesman whose jobs are shoddy.

clue.text: Revolutionary left's main London location

parts.note: Che Guevara was the Argentine revolutionary
the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's principal base in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests a reversal but simply gives CHE. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is an affluent district of west London, on the Thames.

clue.text: Announced device to detect change is cut

indicators.note: announced means the word is spoken, so we want something sounding like it

parts.note: a sensor detects changes such as heat or motion

explanation.surface: A notice that a monitoring gadget has been altered or switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' is a verb: to remove material.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor a text or film is to cut out objectionable parts.

clue.text: Be out rioting around story time in dungeon

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go about the story and time
rioting suggests wild disorder, so the words Be out are scrambled

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Prisoners break out in a riot after a long stretch in the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' turns BE OUT into OUBTE, split around LIE and T. The final 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret dungeon entered only by a trapdoor in its ceiling, from French for 'forget'.

clue.text: Kicks ball over opposition to score headers

indicators.note: headers points to the head, the first letter, of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A footballer kicks the ball past defenders and scores with headers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headers' looks like football, but takes the first letters of ball, over, opposition, to, score.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to boot a ball is to kick it.

clue.text: Shrank length taking in something over a foot

indicators.note: taking in means the words Shrank length hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Trousers that shrank in length now take in something more than twelve inches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over a foot' suggests a measurement of more than twelve inches, but means positioned above the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the joint linking leg and foot sits directly above the foot.

clue.text: Steer game around, holding match

indicators.note: around tells us to read the hidden letters backwards
holding means Steer game contains the letters

explanation.surface: Steering the game round while hanging on to win the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden in 'stEER GAme' and read backwards. 'match' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: two accounts that match agree with each other.

clue.text: Wasted billion on game of chance

parts.note: lotto is a game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A billion squandered on a lottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' looks like spent, but means drunk. 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonyms: wasted and blotto both mean very drunk.

clue.text: Spurs rue playing those who took title

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of Spurs rue are moved around in play

explanation.surface: Tottenham fans regret a match where rivals seized the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper is one who seizes a throne or title without right.

clue.text: Leave middle out of pudding

indicators.note: middle out of says the central letter is removed from the word for pudding

parts.note: pudding is the British word for a dessert

explanation.surface: Leaving the centre of a pudding uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: DESSERT has seven letters; removing its central S gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to desert is to leave or abandon.

clue.text: Unravelling lace? Darn — its days are numbered

indicators.note: unravelling means the threads of lace and Darn come apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lace coming undone despite darning, so its days are numbered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its days are numbered' sounds like doom for the lace but literally describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom read literally: a wall chart of dates has each day printed with a number.
